default_tip: Pick one language (Java or Python) and solve small exercises every day until loops, methods and arrays feel easy.
Build a small app with classes, inheritance and interfaces, for example a library or bank system.
Put all your course projects on GitHub and practise branches, commits and pull requests.
Revise lists, stacks, queues, trees and sorting, then solve easy coding problems on a practice website.
Learn SQL SELECT, JOIN and GROUP BY and design a small database for one of your projects.
Call a free public REST API from code and then build a small API of your own.
Write unit tests for one of your projects using JUnit or pytest.
Make a simple website with HTML, CSS and JavaScript to understand how the web works.
Before coding, write down the steps on paper. Explain your solution to a friend to check it.
Present one of your projects to classmates and write a clear README for it.
Rebuild the layout of a website you like using only HTML and CSS, including flexbox and grid.
Learn variables, functions, arrays and the DOM, then add interactive features to your HTML page.
Host your web projects on GitHub and publish one with GitHub Pages.
Follow the official React tutorial and then build a small to-do or weather app.
Use fetch to get data from a public API and show it on your page.
Learn basic SQL and connect a simple back end to a database.
Make your site work on phone, tablet and laptop sizes using media queries.
Join a group project or hackathon and practise splitting tasks and reviewing code together.
Explain your design choices to a classmate and ask for honest feedback.
Practise formulas, pivot tables and charts with a free public dataset.
Revise mean, median, standard deviation and correlation using real examples.
Practise SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY and subqueries on a sample database.
Learn Python basics and then the pandas library for working with tables.
Take a messy dataset and fix missing values, duplicates and wrong formats.
Make clear charts and pick the right chart type for each question.
Build one dashboard with the free version of Power BI or Tableau Public.
Start each analysis by writing the question you want to answer in one sentence.
Write a short summary of your findings for someone who is not technical.
Practise plans, sections and elevations by hand and check them against drawing standards.
Redraw one of your studio projects in AutoCAD using layers and proper line weights.
Model a small house in Revit and produce plans and sections from the model.
Use SketchUp or Rhino to model and render one of your designs.
Read the main local building code sections on fire safety, access and space standards.
Study built projects you admire and analyse their plans, light and circulation.
Pick your best 5 to 8 projects and make a clean portfolio that tells a story.
Plan studio deadlines backwards from the due date and use breaks for skill practice.
Practise presenting your design in 3 minutes, like in a real client meeting.
Learn Kotlin (Android) or Swift (iOS) basics with small daily exercises.
Build a small app using classes and interfaces, for example a notes app.
Keep every app project on GitHub and practise branches and pull requests.
Follow the official Android or Apple developer tutorials and publish a simple app to your phone.
Try a cross-platform framework by rebuilding one of your apps for both Android and iOS.
Make your app load live data from a free public API.
Save app data locally with SQLite or a simple cloud database.
Write a few unit tests and test your app on different screen sizes.
Break each app feature into small steps before you start coding.
Build an app with a classmate and split the screens between you.
Learn layout, colour, typography and spacing by redesigning an app you use every day.
Interview 3 to 5 people about a problem and write down what they need.
Sketch the main screens of an app on paper before using any tool.
Recreate your wireframes in Figma using frames, components and auto layout.
Link your Figma screens into a clickable prototype.
Watch 3 people use your prototype and note where they get stuck.
Check colour contrast and text sizes against the WCAG guidelines.
Learn enough HTML and CSS to understand how developers build your designs.
Present your design and explain your decisions in a short case study.
Work with a developer classmate and hand over your design files clearly.
